\chapter{Complexity — Oracle Nondeterministic}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.OracleNondeterministic
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.OracleNondeterministic}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Nondeterministic oracle Turing machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b001,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b002
}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
A nondeterministic oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, a symbol
alphabet, and a state set consists of an initial state, a query state, a positive-answer
state, a negative-answer state, and two transition functions indexed by a choice bit.
Each transition function takes a state, the possibly blank symbol under the input head,
and the scanned symbols on the $k$ ordinary work tapes together with the query tape, and
returns a one-step action on those $k+1$ tapes.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Distinct Oracle control states]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.WellFormed}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b001,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b002
}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.WellFormed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM}
An oracle nondeterministic Turing machine is well formed when its query state differs
from each of its positive-answer and negative-answer states, and those two answer states
differ from one another.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Running with an oracle and choice sequence]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b001,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b002
}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleTM.queryString}
Given an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine, an oracle language, a finite sequence
of nondeterministic choice bits, and a configuration, the resulting configuration is
obtained by processing the choice bits in order, applying one oracle-machine step for
each bit.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial machine configuration]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.OracleNDTM}
For an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine and an input string, the initial
configuration is the machine's initial configuration on that input, with the machine's
initial state.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle machine run]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b001,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b002
}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith}
Given an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine, an oracle language, a finite sequence
of nondeterministic choice bits, and an input string, the run is the configuration
obtained by processing those bits in order from the machine's initial configuration on
the input.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Run on an empty choice sequence]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_nil}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_nil}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine, let $O$ be a language over its
symbol alphabet, and let $c$ be a configuration for an input word. Running $N$ with
oracle $O$ on the empty sequence of choice bits leaves $c$ unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One-step expansion of a computation]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_cons}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_cons}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{1}
For an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, an oracle language $O$, a choice bit
$b$, a finite choice sequence $w$, and a configuration $c$, running on the sequence
beginning with $b$ and followed by $w$ gives the same configuration as first taking one
step using $b$ and then running on $w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concatenation of computation sequences]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_append}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_append}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_cons}
\difficulty{4}
For an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, an oracle language $O$, finite choice
sequences $w,w'$, and a configuration $c$, running $N$ with $O$ on the concatenated
sequence $w w'$ from $c$ gives the same configuration as first running it on $w$ from
$c$ and then on $w'$ from the resulting configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Halting configurations are fixed]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_of_halt}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_of_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic oracle Turing machine, $O$ an oracle language, $b$ a
choice bit, and $c$ a configuration with no state. Then the step of $N$ from $c$ using
choice $b$ relative to $O$ leaves $c$ unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A halted configuration remains unchanged]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{4}
For an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, an oracle language $O$, a
configuration $c$ whose state is the halting state, and any finite choice sequence $w$,
running $N$ with $O$ on $w$ from $c$ leaves $c$ unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Halting within a fixed number of steps]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.HaltsWithin}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b002,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b003
}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.HaltsWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith}
An oracle nondeterministic Turing machine halts within $t$ steps on an input, relative
to an oracle language, if every sequence of exactly $t$ nondeterministic choice bits
produces a run whose final configuration has no state.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of Bounded Halting]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.HaltsWithin.mono}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.HaltsWithin.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_append, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine, let $O$ be an oracle language, let
$x$ be an input word, and let $t,t'$ be nonnegative integers. If every binary choice
word of length $t$ makes the run of $N$ with oracle $O$, started on $x$, halt, and $t\le
t'$, then every binary choice word of length $t'$ also makes that run halt.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Finite oracle nondeterministic machine]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleNDTM}
\label{Turing.FinOracleNDTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.WellFormed}
A finite oracle nondeterministic Turing machine over a symbol alphabet consists of a
natural number of ordinary work tapes, a finite state type with decidable equality, and
an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine with those states and one additional query
tape. Its query state and its two answer states are pairwise distinct.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance within a fixed number of steps]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.AcceptsWithin}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b002,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b003
}
\label{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.AcceptsWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith}
A finite oracle nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet accepts a
Boolean input within $t$ steps, relative to an oracle language, if there is a sequence
of exactly $t$ nondeterministic choice bits for which the run halts and its output is
the one-symbol string consisting of true.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of bounded acceptance]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono}
\label{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.FinOracleNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_append, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over Boolean strings,
let $O$ be an oracle language, and let $x$ be an input. If some choice sequence of
length $t$ makes the machine halt with output $[\mathrm{true}]$, then for every $t' \ge
t$ some choice sequence of length $t'$ does so as well.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Decision within a time bound]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.DecidesInTime}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b002,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p002-b003
}
\label{Turing.FinOracleNDTM.DecidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.FinOracleNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.OracleNDTM.HaltsWithin}
A finite oracle nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet decides a
language $L$ in time $T$ relative to an oracle language $O$ if, for every Boolean input
string $x$, every choice sequence of length $T(|x|)$ leads to a halting run with oracle
$O$, and $x$ belongs to $L$ exactly when the machine accepts $x$ within $T(|x|)$ steps
relative to $O$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Deterministic oracle machine as a nondeterministic machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleTM}
Every oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes determines an oracle
nondeterministic Turing machine with the same initial, query, positive-answer, and
negative-answer states, whose transition function is independent of the nondeterministic
choice bit and agrees with the original transition function.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of well-formedness]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM_wellFormed}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM_wellFormed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM.WellFormed, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.WellFormed, Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine whose query state, positive-answer state, and
negative-answer state are pairwise distinct. Then the nondeterministic oracle machine
obtained from $M$ also has pairwise distinct query, positive-answer, and negative-answer
states.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Deterministic and Nondeterministic Step Agreement]
\lean{Turing.toOracleNDTM_stepWith}
\label{Turing.toOracleNDTM_stepWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, alphabet $\Sigma$, and
state set $Q$; let $O$ be a language over $\Sigma$, let $b\in\{0,1\}$, and let $c$ be a
configuration on input $x$ with $k+1$ work tapes. The step of the nondeterministic
machine obtained from $M$, using choice bit $b$ and oracle $O$, produces exactly the
same configuration as one step of $M$ relative to $O$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nondeterministic run agrees with deterministic run]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM_runWith}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM_runWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM, Turing.toOracleNDTM_stepWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, let $O$ be an oracle
language, let $w$ be a finite list of Boolean choices, and let $c$ be a configuration
with $k+1$ work tapes. Running the nondeterministic machine obtained from $M$ on $O$
using the choice list $w$ from $c$ gives the same configuration as running $M$ on $O$
from $c$ for exactly the length of $w$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Fixing a nondeterministic choice]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.fixChoice}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.fixChoice}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleTM}
Given an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes and a fixed
choice bit $b \in \{0,1\}$, fixing that bit yields an oracle Turing machine with the
same initial, query, positive-answer, and negative-answer states, whose transition
function is the original transition function evaluated at $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-choice step equivalence]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.fixChoice, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.toOracleNDTM_stepWith}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic oracle Turing machine, $O$ an oracle language, $b$ a
choice bit, and $c$ a configuration. The step of $N$ using choice $b$ on $c$ relative to
$O$ equals the step of the deterministic oracle machine obtained from $N$ by fixing its
choice to $b$ on $c$ relative to $O$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle independence away from query states]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_of_ne_qQuery}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_of_ne_qQuery}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.fixChoice, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step, Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_ne_qQuery}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic oracle Turing machine, let $O_1$ and $O_2$ be oracle
languages over its symbol alphabet, let $b$ be a choice bit, and let $c$ be a
configuration whose state is not the query state of $N$. Then the step using choice $b$
from $c$ is the same relative to $O_1$ and $O_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Work tape bounds during a run]
\lean{Turing.runWith_headBlank}
\label{Turing.runWith_headBlank}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.fixChoice, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_nil, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step, Turing.OracleTM.step_radius}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine with $k+1$ work tapes, let $O$ be a
language over its symbol alphabet, and let $w$ be a Boolean word specifying the
successive choices in a run from configuration $c$. Suppose that for some $n\in\mathbb
N$, every work-tape head of $c$ is within distance $n$ of the origin, and every cell at
distance at least $n$ from the origin is blank on every work tape. After the run, every
work-tape head is within distance $n+|w|$ of the origin, and every cell at distance at
least $n+|w|$ is blank on every work tape.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Work-tape bounds during a computation]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_workTapes_invariant}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_workTapes_invariant}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.runWith_headBlank}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine, $O$ an oracle language, $x$ an
input word, and $w$ a finite sequence of choice bits. In the resulting configuration,
every work-tape head is within distance $|w|$ of cell $0$. Moreover, for every work tape
and every integer cell position $z$ with $|w|\le |z|$, that cell is blank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query length bounded by the computation length]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.queryString_runWith_length_le}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.queryString_runWith_length_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_workTapes_invariant, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le_of_blank}
\difficulty{1}
For an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, an oracle language $O$, an input word
$x$, and a finite sequence $w$ of nondeterministic choice bits, the query word on the
final query tape after running $N$ with $O$ from its initial configuration on $x$ has
length at most $|w|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Finite deterministic oracle machine as a nondeterministic machine]
\lean{Turing.FinOracleTM.toFinOracleNDTM}
\label{Turing.FinOracleTM.toFinOracleNDTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinOracleNDTM, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM, Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM_wellFormed}
Every well-formed finite oracle Turing machine over a symbol alphabet determines a
well-formed finite oracle nondeterministic Turing machine over the same alphabet. The
resulting machine has the same number of ordinary work tapes and the same finite state
set, and its transition function is independent of the nondeterministic choice bit and
agrees with the original machine's transition function.
\end{definition}
